title: DealSnapshot — Historical Pipeline Ledger
purpose: A per-deal, point-in-time snapshot table for the AgentSwitch CRM. Every time it runs, the rotting-deals agent (or a scheduled AgentTask) writes one row capturing the deal's stage, stage-transition history, and a computed rot score as they stood at that moment — so pipeline health can be queried and trended with plain SQL/report calls, instead of only being recomputed live from Deal + Activity on every question.

source_adaptation.reference_model: MSME CRM's standalone `opportunities` table + a Postgres JSONB snapshot/rot-score side table.

field_mapping.current_stage (TEXT, free-text stage nam: current_stage (type=state, flow=DealFlow, states: new/qualification/proposal/negotiation/closed_won/closed_lost) — reuses Deal's own flow instead of inventing a parallel stage vocabulary
field_mapping.stage_history (JSONB array): stage_history (type=code, same array-of-transitions shape, stage names swapped to DealFlow states)
field_mapping.custom_fields (JSONB object: scenario_ta: custom_fields (type=code) — same idea, deal_amount_inr replaced by a currency-aware {value, currency} pair (AgentSwitch is multi-currency; the reference dataset was INR-only), installation_type dropped (motor/product-specific, not meaningful for a generic Deal), lost_reason left in place (Deal already has its own lost_reason field — the snapshot copy freezes what it was AT CAPTURE TIME, in case the live Deal record is edited later)
field_mapping.rot_score (NUMERIC(4,3)): rot_score (type=number) — same formula, same weights, ported as-is (see rot_score_model)
field_mapping.rot_comment (TEXT): rot_comment (type=text) — same one-line dominant-component explanation, ported as-is

key_differences_from_reference: No opportunity_activity side table exists in AgentSwitch — 'days since last activity' is computed from the existing Activity entity (filters: deal_id, done=true, sort by due_date desc) instead of a bespoke activity log.

The reference `dummy_snapshot` has exactly one row per opportunity and no capture timestamp — despite its name, it behaves as a current-state cache, not a time series. Since the brief here is explicitly 'store historical information', this schema adds `captured_at` and `snapshot_reason` so multiple snapshots can accumulate per deal over time; the natural key becomes (deal_id, captured_at), not deal_id alone.

Denormalizes company_id, party_id, owner, pipeline and probability at capture time (reference kept these inside custom_fields only, or relied on a live join to `opportunities`) — a snapshot table should freeze the facts it cares about, not silently re-derive them from a Deal record that may have since changed.

AgentSwitch already computes a simpler two-value rot signal on Deal.list itself (_rot_level: fresh/aging/stale/none, _rot_days, threshold from CRMPreferences.deal_rot_days). DealSnapshot.rot_score is a richer, five-component weighted score for trend analysis and does not replace that field — the two are complementary (see rot_score_model.relationship_to_platform_rot_level).

fields.name: company_id
fields.description: Tenant scope, denormalized at capture time (matches every other entity's multi-tenant pattern).

fields.name: deal_id
fields.description: The deal this snapshot describes. Many rows per deal over time.

fields.name: captured_at
fields.description: When this snapshot was taken. Forms the time axis; (deal_id, captured_at) is the effective natural key.

fields.name: snapshot_reason
fields.description: Why this row exists: a recurring AgentTask sweep, a Deal.stage transition trigger, right before an AgentEscalation was raised, or a manual pull.

fields.name: captured_by
fields.description: Actor that wrote the row — an AgentPersona name, AgentTask id, or a user id for manual captures.

fields.name: current_stage
fields.description: Deal.stage as of captured_at. Reuses the platform's own DealFlow rather than a parallel vocabulary.

fields.name: party_id
fields.description: Deal.party_id at capture time (denormalized so history survives the deal being reassigned).

fields.name: currency
fields.description: Deal.currency at capture time (replaces the reference's INR-only deal_amount_inr).

fields.name: expected_close_date
fields.description: Deal.expected_close_date at capture time — compared against captured_at to derive the slippage component.

fields.name: stage_history
fields.description: JSON array of stage transitions up to captured_at. See stage_history_shape below.

fields.name: custom_fields
fields.description: JSON object of scenario/risk metadata. See custom_fields_shape below.

fields.name: has_regressed
fields.description: True if stage_history contains a transition with event='regression' (the deal moved backward in DealFlow, e.g. negotiation -> qualification).

fields.name: days_since_last_activity
fields.description: Raw input behind activity_score — days between captured_at and the most recent done=true Activity linked to this deal.

fields.name: rot_score
fields.description: 0 (fresh) to 1 (fully rotten). NULL for closed_won/closed_lost deals — see rot_score_model.

fields.name: rot_comment
fields.description: One-line explanation naming the dominant component behind rot_score (stage time, inactivity, slippage, regression, or deal value).

item_shape.stage: one of DealFlow's states: new | qualification | proposal | negotiation | closed_won | closed_lost
item_shape.entered_at: ISO date the deal entered this stage
item_shape.days_in_stage: integer — how long it stayed there before the next transition (or, for the last entry, days up to captured_at)
item_shape.event: optional — 'regression' when this transition moved the deal backward relative to DealFlow's normal forward order (new -> qualification -> proposal -> negotiation -> closed_won/closed_lost)

keys.scenario_tag: human-readable bucket for reporting/testing, e.g. 'Healthy Progression', 'Stalled - At Risk', 'Ghost - No Engagement', 'Regressed Deal', 'High Value - At Risk', 'Fast Track - Hot Deal', 'Closed Won - Efficient Cycle', 'Closed Lost - Lost to Competitor' (ported verbatim from the reference dataset's scenario taxonomy)
keys.risk_flag: bool — quick filter, true when rot_score >= rot_score_model.thresholds.at_risk
keys.days_stuck: integer — days_in_current_stage at capture time (denormalized copy of the last stage_history entry's days_in_stage for easy SQL filtering without unpacking JSON)
keys.last_activity_days_ago: integer or null — same value as the top-level days_since_last_activity field, kept here too for parity with the reference's custom_fields shape
keys.competitor_won: text or null — populated only when stage=closed_lost and the deal was lost to a named competitor
keys.lost_reason: text or null — snapshot-time copy of Deal.lost_reason
keys.value_at_capture: { "value": number, "currency": text } — duplicate of the top-level value/currency fields, kept nested for parity with the reference's embedded deal_amount_inr and for JSONB-containment queries
keys.notes: free-text one-liner summarizing why this snapshot looks the way it does

rot_score_model.ported_from: src/msmecrmapp/pipeline_health/data.py: compute_rot_scores() / ROT_SCORE_WEIGHTS / _rot_comment() — formula and weights carried over unchanged, only the input queries change (see inputs_in_agentswitch).

components.S_stage: min(days_in_current_stage / (2 * median_days_for_that_stage_among_closed_won_deals), 1) — a deal sitting in a stage twice as long as a typical won deal maxes this out.
components.S_activity: min(days_since_last_activity / 30, 1) — days since the most recent done=true Activity linked to the deal.
components.S_regression: 1 if has_regressed else 0 — any backward transition in stage_history.
components.S_value: min(deal.value / p90(value among all open deals), 1) — bigger deals rot 'louder'.

rot_score_model.scope: Open deals only — stage not in [closed_won, closed_lost]. rot_score/rot_comment are left NULL for closed deals, exactly as in the reference.

inputs_in_agentswitch.days_in_current_stage: from the last entry of this row's own stage_history
inputs_in_agentswitch.median_days_for_that_stage: computed once, offline, from stage_history of DealSnapshot rows whose deal_id's Deal.stage = closed_won — same 'baseline from won deals' idea as the reference's fetch_closed_won_stage_history()
inputs_in_agentswitch.days_since_last_activity: report(entity=Activity, aggregate=max, field=due_date, group_by=deal_id, filters={deal_id, done:true}) via the agent_tools.json `report` tool, or Activity.list(filters={deal_id, done:true}, sort_by=due_date, sort_order=desc, limit=1)
inputs_in_agentswitch.has_regressed: any stage_history entry with event='regression' for this deal, up to captured_at
inputs_in_agentswitch.deal.value / p90(value): Deal.value for this row vs. the 90th percentile of value across all currently-open deals, via report(entity=Deal, aggregate=max/avg as a p90 proxy or computed client-side from list(...))

rot_score_model.relationship_to_platform_rot_level: AgentSwitch's own Deal.list already returns a computed `_rot_level` (fresh/aging/stale/none) and `_rot_days`, driven purely by elapsed time against CRMPreferences.deal_rot_days — a single threshold, no activity/slippage/regression/value weighting, and not persisted anywhere (recomputed on every read). DealSnapshot.rot_score is the richer, multi-factor score from the reference model, persisted so it can be trended over time and queried without recomputation; the two numbers will usually agree on direction but not on scale, and a report built on this table should not conflate them.

sql_ddl_postgres:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deals_snapshot (
    id                        UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    company_id                UUID NOT NULL,
    deal_id                   UUID NOT NULL,
    captured_at                TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    snapshot_reason           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (snapshot_reason IN ('scheduled','stage_transition','escalation','manual')),
    captured_by               TEXT,
    current_stage             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (current_stage IN ('new','qualification','proposal','negotiation','closed_won','closed_lost')),
    party_id                  UUID,
    owner                     TEXT,
    pipeline                  TEXT,
    value                     NUMERIC(18,2),
    currency                  TEXT,
    probability                NUMERIC(5,2),
    expected_close_date        DATE,
    stage_history              JSONB,
    custom_fields              JSONB,
    has_regressed              BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    days_since_last_activity   INTEGER,
    rot_score                 NUMERIC(4,3) CHECK (rot_score IS NULL OR (rot_score >= 0 AND rot_score <= 1)),
    rot_comment                TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_deals_snapshot_deal_id ON deals_snapshot (deal_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_deals_snapshot_deal_captured ON deals_snapshot (deal_id, captured_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_deals_snapshot_current_stage ON deals_snapshot (current_stage);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_deals_snapshot_rot_score ON deals_snapshot (rot_score) WHERE rot_score IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_deals_snapshot_stage_history_gin ON deals_snapshot USING GIN (stage_history);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_deals_snapshot_custom_fields_gin ON deals_snapshot USING GIN (custom_fields);

custom_fields.notes: No expected_close_date set and no Activity logged since creation — real note comment, not from live data.

sample_rows.rot_comment: Not scored yet: no Activity exists to anchor days_since_last_activity (illustrative row — real scoring requires at least one Activity or an explicit null-activity handling rule).

custom_fields.notes: Illustrative worked example (§4 of docs/crm_gapreport.md) — SuryaTools Nashik ITI bulk order sitting in negotiation well past the typical cycle, with a month of silence.

sample_rows.rot_comment: Primarily driven by time in current stage: 46 days in negotiation vs. a ~20-day median for won deals (rot score 0.59).

custom_fields.notes: Real deal from deallist.json — closed_lost is out of rot_score scope per the model.

indexes: btree(deal_id, captured_at DESC) — fetch a deal's latest or full history fast
partial btree(rot_score) WHERE rot_score IS NOT NULL — open-pipeline rot queries skip closed rows entirely
row_count_plan: Unlike the reference's fixed 180-row, one-per-opportunity dummy_snapshot, this table grows over time: one row per open Deal per scheduled sweep (e.g. weekly via AgentTask), plus one row per Deal on every stage transition and every AgentEscalation raised. Expect roughly (open_deal_count * sweeps_per_period) + (stage_transitions) + (escalations) rows per period — prune or partition by captured_at once retention policy is decided (AgentRetentionRule/LedgerRetentionPolicy already exist on the platform for exactly this purpose).
notes: This is a proposed schema, not a live AgentSwitch entity — it does not yet exist in document/schemas.json. Per docs/crm_gapreport.md §2b, adding it (a new table + write path) is backend work; the agent's existing 13-tool seat can compute everything in rot_score_model.inputs_in_agentswitch on the fly, this table just persists the result so it can be trended and queried without recomputation.

kind='ledger' matches the platform's own convention for append-only, system-written history tables (e.g. AgentRunbookRun, LedgerRetentionEvent) — permissions are read-only for business roles; only the agent/system actor writes rows.

current_stage reuses Deal's own DealFlow rather than the reference's free-text stage names (Prospecting/Proposal Sent/Verbal Commit/…), so stage_history stays queryable against the same flow the rest of the platform already understands.
'Verbal Commit' from the reference's STAGE_ORDER has no equivalent in DealFlow (new -> qualification -> proposal -> negotiation -> closed_won/closed_lost) and was dropped rather than invented.
'installation_type' from the reference's custom_fields was dropped — it's a motor/product-install attribute specific to the MSME manufacturing dataset, with no analogue on the generic Deal entity.
